title: Hosted 5xx escalation: automated triage + staged hotpatch and safe fallback
creator: Ethan Liu
description:
Summary: Multiple customers reported sustained waves of 5xxs and timeouts for Hosted inference starting 2026-03-08 22:15 UTC. This ticket bundles the post-triage corrective work: an automated escalation triage helper, a staged hotpatch that applies an inflight-cap throttle + idempotency shim, and telemetry/alert changes to prevent repeat regressions. The goal is to restore customer-facing throughput within SLA while avoiding retry-amplification loops and preserving signal for downstream debugging.

Why this is distinct: previous tickets focused on ad-hoc backoff or tenant quarantine. Here we introduce an automated per-tenant admission gate that (a) detects retry-amplification patterns via request-id correlation, (b) applies a temporary inflight cap with graceful 429-like metadata to SDKs, and (c) rolls in a non-disruptive K/V cache eviction guard to prevent compaction storms during tenant surges. This ticket coordinates Hosted, Dedicated and Private guardrails but implements the immediate fix for Hosted runtime instability.
investigation_notes:
Timeline and signals observed:
- 2026-03-08 22:15 UTC: first customer report (mobile app) showing partial responses and 502/504 envelope errors.
- 22:18: backlog spike on frontdoor connection queue (edge metrics).
- 22:20: KV-cache eviction rate increases 6x on affected shards; kernel hot path logs show increased _batch size variance_.
- 22:21: repeated client retries with identical request-id observed; connection churn increased.
- 22:24: several internal SDKs misconfigured keepalive -> long-lived connections exposed to proxies, causing pooled file-descriptor pressure.
Root cause hypothesis: combined effect of (1) client retry storms with no idempotency tokens, (2) edge connection pool fragmentation causing backend probes to queue, and (3) kv-cache compaction that turned small stalls into larger synchronous slowpaths, producing 502/504s and cascading retries.
Repro: synthetic tenant replay against staging with high retry probability reproduced same k/v eviction pattern and subsequent timeouts.
Key traces: trace IDs and example calls are saved in the incident dashboard (links below).
mitigation_patch:
Patch summary (hotpatch v1):
- inbound request admission controller: enforce per-tenant 'inflight' semaphore (default=40) on Hosted. Semaphore is token-based, best-effort, non-persistent. Excess requests return 429-equivalent metadata header 'X-RWI-Retry-After' with suggested backoff.
- idempotency shim: if client provides idempotency-key header, map to request dedup table for 30s to absorb duplicates for short replays.
- KV-cache compaction guard: when eviction rate exceeds threshold, switch to async compaction mode for 90s to avoid synchronous stalls.
- connection pool tuning: lower edge proxy keepalive concurrency for long-lived streams; add liveness probe to gracefully drain stale sockets.
Implementation notes: changes are feature-flagged (ff-hosted-inflight) and default off for Dedicated/Private. Hotpatch applies to Hosted edge and runtime nodes only.
Rollout plan: Canary to 3% of Hosted nodes for 30 minutes, inspect telemetry, then 25%, then full.
Backout: toggle feature flag off and revert semaphores; KV compaction guard is reversible via config toggle.
rollforward_plan:
- Canary: enable ff-hosted-inflight on canary edge and 2 runtime pods 2026-03-15 14:00 UTC; monitor 5xx rate, queue depth, kvcache eviction, p99 latency.
- Automatic guard: if 5xx rate reduces by >= 60% for canary over 20m window and no new regressions on latency, increase to 25% (2026-03-15 15:00 UTC).
- Full rollout: staged increments to 100%, each step validated via automated smoke tests and synthetic tenant load harness.
- Post-rollout: create follow-up to tune default semaphore and idempotency TTL for workload profiles.
rollback_plan:
- Immediate: disable ff-hosted-inflight (feature flag) and revert connection pool keepalive change.
- If disabling flag doesn't reduce 5xx: rollback KV compaction guard; if still not stable, scale up ingest capacity and trigger tenant soft-quarantine (manual).
- Post-mortem: if rollback required, collect full traces and run root-cause regression test in staging to validate fix cannot be re-applied safely.
telemetry_changes:
Alerts and dashboards updated:
- New alert 'Hosted: Retry-amplification index' (ratio of repeated request-id within 60s) -> PagerDuty P0.
- Add histogram for per-tenant inflight counts and eviction-rate spike detector.
- Instrument idempotency-dedup hit/miss counters and surface via Console per-tenant diagnostics.
- SDK guidance: publish a note to SDK repo and docs to recommend idempotency-key usage and exponential backoff.
- Logging: add structured field 'rwi_inflight_reason' when admissions throttle is applied.
Monitoring links are attached in links[].
decision: Go-forward: ship hotpatch v1 to Hosted only, with feature flag and controlled canary. Do NOT apply to Dedicated/Private until we validate resource isolation assumptions (private networks may have different connection dynamics). Team agreed this morning in incident bridge (Ethan, Priya, Mateo, Anika).
next_steps:
- PR: create runtime patch PR in github.com/redwood-inference/runtime (PR #3246).
- Ops: coordinate canary window with SRE; schedule post-rollout oncall handoff.
- SDK: add idempotency examples to node and python SDKs; update docs.
- Post-mortem: schedule 90-minute blameless review and publish learned mitigations in Confluence.
- Follow-up: evaluate automatic idempotency generation and smarter kernel scheduling to reduce compaction coupling.
review_feedback:
- Security: quick check on idempotency table key length and potential DoS vector (requested by security review; short TTL enforced).
- SRE: asked for additional guard to limit feature-flagged canary to tenants with <10% traffic share to avoid noisy neighbor effect.
- Product: requested customer comms template for impacted customers with timeline and mitigation steps.
Feedback actions: added short TTL and tenant-share gating to rollout plan; PM draft for customer notice created.
customer_comms: Draft sent to CX: brief summary of root cause, immediate mitigations, expected timeline for fix, and suggested retry guidance for customers. Template stored in Confluence link above. Customer-facing affected list captured in Drive folder.
